subject.title: feat: add interactive launcher menu as thin wrapper over existing CLI

question: Should OpenClaw core own and release a standalone Rust launcher as an additional public command-dispatch surface?
rationale: The repository already has canonical CLI and companion-app launch paths, so accepting another executable creates a permanent product, packaging, and compatibility contract that code review cannot authorize.

options.title: Use existing launch surfaces
options.body: Decline the standalone core launcher and improve bare `openclaw` or the owned companion apps when launch ergonomics need work.

options.title: Sponsor a core launcher
options.body: Approve the Rust executable as a maintained product surface, then require scope cleanup, native discovery, packaging ownership, and cross-platform proof.

options.title: Maintain it externally
options.body: Distribute the launcher as a community application that delegates to the public CLI without adding a core build and release obligation.

recommendation.title: Use existing launch surfaces
recommendation.body: Decline the standalone core launcher and improve bare `openclaw` or the owned companion apps when launch ergonomics need work.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history and policy signals connect this person to repository-level product, setup, and packaging decisions.
